split.plus_en: Broader powers for police, prison service and security forces to arrest, detain, search, monitor and use force; fewer limits on them
split.minus_en: More limits and oversight on police force, searches and dispersal of protests
split.statement_en: The police and security forces should be given broader powers to arrest, search, monitor and use force, even if the risk of abuse grows.

split.name_en: Punitive measures against terrorists and their families
split.plus_en: Deportation of terrorists' families, demolition of their homes, loss of residency, prison for minors convicted of terror, new terror-incitement offences
split.minus_en: No collective or added sanctions beyond the ordinary criminal process
split.statement_en: Israel should impose tougher measures on terrorists and their families, such as deportation, even if relatives who took no part are punished.

reason: About 64% of the listed weight is police/enforcement powers (organized crime, illegal weapons, arrest until end of proceedings, electronic monitoring of protection-order subjects, protest dispersal, strip search, body cameras, police violence) and matches q47; 'monitor' added to cover the electronic-monitoring and computer-access bills. About 36% is a distinct issue: sanctions on terrorists and their families (deportation of families, rows 1/5/10, the single heaviest bill; juvenile terror sentencing; residency; house demolition; incitement). A voter can back one and reject the other, and the current wording (arrest, search, force) does not describe deporting families, so split. Off: tobacco enforcement (13), penal code amendment 150 (14, content unclear from title), UNRWA activity ban (29).
